_note: The Spec §12.3 acceptance table for the pilot document, written from the spec BEFORE the M2b ingest runs — which is the whole of C10. The table is normative for TC1E-SF: if the first real ingest disagrees, that is a blocking finding (offset or tokenisation) until proven a corpus difference, and changing a number here requires a recorded rationale in the run report. Authoring it after the ingest would let the safety net re-baseline itself against whatever the run happened to produce.
_status: awaiting the U013 re-bill. The three artefacts beside this one — raw_window_1.json, raw_window_2.json, text.json — are what the one paid ingest buys (§12.1, OQ-1/OQ-2). Until they exist, the L2 suite that reads this file asserts the table's own shape and skips the corpus rows by name.

corpus.why_the_revision: impl's r-poc-5 manifest publishes TC1E-SF at 1.3, and §5.1 makes the operator's declared revision authoritative. A re-bill under a different revision is a different document to §6.7's retirement, not a new run of this one.

lookup.label: SF 1.1A
lookup.why: §12.3's first row. Any-order matching would return 3 pages — the tokens sf, 1 and 1a occur together on pages that never print the phrase. F1.

lookup.label: SF 121.1
lookup.why: §12.3 — reached through the whitespace-removed variant of §5.6, because the page prints the compact form. F3.

lookup.label: EAO 84-5140.0020
lookup.why: §12.3 states this row as `total 10 (hits capped at cap, capped:true)`. SA-7: at the default cap=20 a total of 10 cannot be capped — §7.1 and §7.2.2 both define `capped` as `total > cap`, and `hits` is the whole set here. The parenthetical is a table-authoring defect, reconciled under C10 in favour of §7.1's definition, which is the one the response model enforces. The count of 10 is unchanged and stays normative.

lookup.label: B&R X20SI4100
lookup.why: §12.3 — 54 > 20, so `hits` is one page of the set and `capped` says so. `total` is the SET size, not len(hits) (§7.1). The ampersand is a punctuation shape the old identifier grammar handled and the phrase index must handle through tokenisation alone.

§12.3 — at ANY cap. `weak` is computed from the server constant WEAK_ABS=20 and the scope's page count, never from the caller's `cap`: a trust signal a client parameter can flip is worse than none (§7.1).

lookup.label: alarm 152
lookup.why: §12.3 — never a wrong page and never a bare empty 200. The tokens are in the corpus and the phrase is not, so the status is honest and `next.suggest` stops the agent abstaining on a phrasing accident.

verify.why: §12.3 — the tokens are present on the page and the phrase is not. One `exact_filter` answers `verify` and `lookup`, which is why F2 cannot disagree with F1 (I3).

not_searchable.why: §12.3's last row and F4 — a page with no text layer answers `not_searchable`, never `not_found`. `grounded_rate` is None there and every aggregate ignores it (§5.7); a fully scanned document publishes and answers not_searchable rather than being quarantined.
not_searchable.expected_from_the_ingest: the page numbers, if any, that probe reports has_text=false. TC1E-SF is born-digital in impl's manifest, so the M2b run is expected to report 0 — recorded here after the ingest, as a measurement rather than a prediction.

parity.rule: every identifier the old entity_keys gate accepted for TC1E-SF is still findable by phrase, on the REAL text this ingest extracts rather than on the projection U012 asserts against
parity.gains: a code the old grammar dropped but the phrase index finds is a GAIN — record it, never reconcile it as a diff (§12.3, verbatim)

negative_set.rule: every raw in withheld.jsonl is UNFINDABLE in the `text` surface — reachable only through include_unverified, always verified:false (I2, F14)

gates.grounded_rate: measured, not predicted — the distribution is reported by `python -m vsir.eval.grounded_rate` and R4 sets the pin from it. Recorded here after the ingest with the run report's rationale.
